source_claims.statement: WordPress recon via robots.txt and sitemaps. Common LFI tests failed with 403/422. Discovered ninja_table_force_download action with url parameter from JS and blog samples.
Extracted nonce from JavaScript. Used AJAX endpoint. Retrieved /etc/os-release.

research_questions.formulation: After common LFI surfaces return 403, does a plugin-specific AJAX action that accepts a url parameter allow file read once a public nonce is supplied?
research_questions.anchor: shift from generic LFI to ninja_table_force_download after JS clue
research_questions.uncertainty_reduced: whether the download action is protected only by nonce
research_questions.assumption_challenged: that 403 on common paths closes file-read possibilities

environment_model_updates: Ninja Tables plugin exposes force_download action
Public nonce required and present in JS
Some paths blocked by WAF (403) vs validation (422)

systematic_vs_exploratory.exploratory: examining blog posts and JS for less obvious download actions

unobserved_history: exact order of file paths tested
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat 403 as proof of no file read
Nonce was a prerequisite that was recoverable from client-side
next_evidence_actions: Note HackerOne program and responsible disclosure
layer_b_candidate_principles: When common LFI paths are blocked, examine plugin-specific AJAX actions and client-side nonces that may unlock them
Distinguish WAF blocks (403) from application validation (422) when interpreting failures
model_vs_harness: Recognizing a plugin action from JS/blog is model reasoning; WordPress endpoint enumeration and nonce extraction can be harness.
